chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, all from al-Hajjal, from Thal'ah, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
‘You should consume endive, for it increases semen, improves the child, and it is hot and moist, increasing in male children.’

key_terms.الْمَاءِ: Semen (in the context of reproductive health)
key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءِ: Endive, a type of leafy green vegetable
key_terms.لَيِّنٌ: Moist/Soft (one of the four humors/ temperaments)

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of endive according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prescribes endive (al-hindaba') as a therapeutic agent, highlighting its 'hot and moist' temperament in the context of traditional Shia medicine (Tibb al-Nabawi) to enhance fertility and specifically increase the likelihood of male offspring. This recommendation reflects the broader scholarly tradition of utilizing dietary remedies for reproductive health, linking physical constitution to spiritual and familial continuity.
